summary: Chat 1 Tablet candidate shard is complete and zero-loss at its recorded base. It reused the existing Tablet census, applied Atlasfin-first conservatively, kept Materiality Catalog in standby, minted no canonical IDs, and wrote only the owned Tablet candidate shard. A bounded current-main authority drift check is the next coordination step before integration consumes the shard.
findings: Tablet Target Index contained 933 records at the lane base: 929 VISUAL_CONTROL_CENSUS_TARGET inputs and 4 existing non-census exact targets excluded from worker input.
Chat 1 reconciled all 929 census inputs exactly once: 139 candidate outcomes, 788 unresolved outcomes, and 2 conflicts.
Physical status at the lane base: 927 CURRENT and 2 DRIFT; all 929 source/output projection relationships were CURRENT against the governing visual-source manifest.
Atlasfin-first accounting: 138 MATCHED_RECIPE, 789 NO_MATCH, and 2 NOT_APPLICABLE because physical evidence was in DRIFT.
NDC remained UNRESOLVED for all 929 records because no direct existing NDC authority relation was proven; no NDC meaning was inferred from selector names.
One existing resolved Identity binding was reused only on exact selector plus implementationLayerId equality.
The two physical conflicts are TGT.CENSUS.TABLET.3B2FED34BC21B5C9FEEC.V1 and TGT.CENSUS.TABLET.850AD4CEF4CCD12BCD05.V1.
decisions: Reuse current Target Index and expanded Visual Control evidence; do not run broad rediscovery.
Use Atlasfin as priority visual reference but promote only evidence-backed recipe-level candidates; do not guess family or preset variants.
Do not inspect or fall back to the Surface Visual Governor Materiality Catalog; keep it STANDBY_USER_INVOKED_ONLY.
Preserve null/UNRESOLVED values where current machine authority is ambiguous; unknown stays unknown.
Do not mint canonical NDC, VIS, BND, TGT, LYR, Identity recipe/family/preset, or adapter IDs from the surface worker.
Treat lane output as candidate exchange data only, never as Work Entry authorization, GVAE receipt, runtime certification, or canonical authority.
